hook: 84% survival rate — but only when caught early.
caption: Oral cancer has one of the starkest early-detection gaps in oncology. Caught in its early stages, the five-year survival rate climbs to around 84%. Caught late, that number drops below 40%. The difference often comes down to whether someone noticed a symptom and acted on it. A sore that won't heal, a patch that looks different, a lump you can feel but can't explain — these aren't things to wait out for months. OralCheck's free screener takes a few minutes and helps you figure out whether what you're seeing is worth a closer look. Start your free risk check at oralcheck.org.
